summary: Slack provides a structured process for app development and distribution. Developers can use the Slack CLI or dashboard to create apps, which require workspace association. Public distribution involves meeting specific prerequisites, security guidelines, and a formal review process.

reason.text: The Slack CLI and dashboard provide clear paths for creating and running a new app project.
reason.label: inferred
reason.note: Model judgement from the verified claims in this guide; not tested.

reason.text: Public distribution requires meeting multiple prerequisites, including a 10-workspace installation threshold and a lengthy functional review process.
reason.label: inferred
reason.note: Model judgement from the verified claims in this guide; not tested.

claim.text: You must associate a Slack app with a workspace when you create it.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: When you create a Slack app, you associate it with a workspace: to do this, open the app dashboard for your app and click Install App to Workspace within the Install App section.

claim.text: Apps intended for commercial distribution must be submitted and approved for listing in the Slack Marketplace.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: apps intended for commercial distribution should be submitted and approved for listing in the Slack Marketplace.

claim.text: Apps open to installation by other workspaces must support SSL for specific URLs.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Your app must support SSL for all of the following URLs: OAuth redirect URLs Request URLs for interaction payloads from interactive components, actions and slash commands Block Kit interactive component options load URLs Events API request URLs

claim.text: Apps must be installed on 10 or more active workspaces before submission.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Your app has been installed on 10 or more active workspaces and the service has been tested on those workspaces in accordance with the above bullet.

claim.text: Apps must meet specific prerequisites before they can be submitted for review.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Review process: What happens after you submit your app, including the prerequisites your app needs to meet before review and how to prepare for a smooth submission.

claim.text: Apps are checked against guidelines covering suitability, functionality, security, design, and listing details.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Submission guidelines and requirements: The guidelines we check your app against during review, covering app suitability, functionality, security, design, and the details of your listing.

limits.item: The temporary authorization code expires after ten minutes.

claim.text: The temporary authorization code expires after ten minutes.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Parse the HTTP request that lands at your Redirect URL for a code field. That's your temporary authorization code, which expires after ten minutes.

claim.text: A single token may set 30 user profiles per minute.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: And a single token may only set 30 user profiles per minute.

claim.text: The rate limit for posting messages is one per second per channel.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: In general, apps may post no more than one message per second per channel, whether a message is posted via chat.postMessage, an incoming webhook, or one of the many other ways to send messages in to Slack.

claim.text: Updating a user's profile is limited to 10 times per minute per token.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: A token may update a single user's profile no more than 10 times per minute.

claim.text: Workflow triggers for events are limited to 10,000 per hour.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote:
Workflow triggers: event triggers
10,000 per hour

claim.text: Workflow triggers for webhooks are limited to 10 per minute.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote:
Workflow triggers: webhook triggers
10 per minute

claim.text: RTM websocket URL requests are limited to 1 per minute.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Limit requests to these methods to no more than 1 per minute, with some bursting behavior allowed.

claim.text: You cannot disable distribution once your app is published in the Slack Marketplace.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Note that you cannot disable distribution in this way once your app is published within the Slack Marketplace; instead, you must discontinue your listing there.

claim.text: Certain app-level configurations cannot be turned off once enabled.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: oauth_config.token_management_enabled App-level config, takes effect for new token issuance. Cannot be turned off once enabled. oauth_config.pkce_enabled App-level config, takes effect for new OAuth flows. Cannot be turned off once enabled.

blockers.issue: You must use HTTPS for your redirect URI.

claim.text: You must use HTTPS for your redirect URI.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: The redirect_uri must use HTTPS. Alternatively, you can configure a Redirect URL in the App Management page under OAuth & Permissions. A Redirect URL must also use HTTPS.

blockers.issue: A bad_redirect_uri error occurs if the redirect_uri parameter does not match the…

claim.text: A bad_redirect_uri error occurs if the redirect_uri parameter does not match the configured Redirect URL or if multiple values are provided that do not match.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: When there are multiple Redirect URL values configured, the redirect_url parameter must be sent in both the Authorize and Access steps described below, and the parameter value must be the same for both steps — otherwise, you will encounter a bad_redirect_uri error:

blockers.issue: You cannot combine Sign in with Slack user scopes with non-Sign in with Slack scopes in…

claim.text: You cannot combine Sign in with Slack user scopes with non-Sign in with Slack scopes in the same OAuth flow.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: A scope conflict occurs when attempting to combine Sign in with Slack (SIWS) user scopes with non-Sign in with Slack scopes in the same OAuth flow

blockers.fix: Limit messages to 4000 characters or split the message into multiple parts.

claim.text: Sending a message longer than 16 kilobytes via RTM will cause the client to be disconnected.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: The message server will disconnect any client that sends a message longer than 16 kilobytes.

blockers.fix: Stop sending messages when rate limits are exceeded.

claim.text: Continuing to send messages after exceeding a rate limit on RTM risks permanent app disablement.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Continuing to send messages after exceeding a rate limit runs the risk of your app being permanently disabled.

blockers.fix: Test your app fully before upgrading.

claim.text: Upgrading to granular permissions cannot be undone.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Note: Upgrading to granular permissions is a fundamental change to your app. It cannot be undone.

blockers.issue: Slack apps cannot access the Real Time Messaging API.
blockers.fix: If you require access to RTM, you'll need to create a legacy Slack app and use its bot token to call rtm.connect.

claim.text: Slack apps cannot access the Real Time Messaging API.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Slack apps cannot access the Real Time Messaging (RTM) API

claims.text: Slack apps can use three different types of tokens.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: Understand the different types of tokens your app can use (user tokens, bot tokens, and app tokens) and how to manage them, as well as employ token rotation and expiry to keep things fresh.

claims.text: You can choose between undistributed apps that reside in a single workspace or distributed apps that can be installed on multiple workspaces.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: When you create a Slack app, it resides in one workspace. You can also distribute Slack apps in either listed or unlisted fashion.

claims.text: Undistributed apps are limited to a single workspace and cannot be distributed to others.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: Undistributed apps exist on a single workspace and can use the full range of app capabilities, but they can't be distributed to other workspaces.

claims.text: Distributed apps require an OAuth 2.0 flow to generate access tokens for each workspace and user.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: Installing your app on other workspaces means that you'll need to set up an OAuth 2.0 flow. Once you've done that, your app will be able to generate access tokens for each workspace and user.

claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: OAuth tokens do not expire. If they are no longer needed, they can be revoked.

claims.text: Submitting your app to the Slack Marketplace is recommended for apps intended for commercial distribution.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: You can also go a step further and submit your app to the Slack Marketplace. This is recommended for apps intended for commercial distribution.
